title: Unit modulus of powers of a root of unity
statement: Fix an integer $k \ge 1$ and write $\omega_k = e^{2\pi i/k}$ for the primitive $k$-th root of unity. For every residue $a \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$, the complex number $\omega_k^{a}$, obtained by raising $\omega_k$ to the canonical representative of $a$ in $\{0,\dots,k-1\}$, satisfies $\norm{\omega_k^{a}} = 1$, so it lies on the unit circle.
hypotheses_covered: k is a positive natural number (NeZero k)
a is an element of Z/kZ
replaced:
For every $a : \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$, $\|\omega_k^a\| = 1$; the image of
$\texttt{ZkFourier.toOmega}$ lies on the complex unit circle.
